## Parent

- Slice 2A implementation plan, section 2.2 (ranking config, formula, worked example) and ticket R2: https://github.com/devuser/Lumen/blob/7bbf8a58f8e2b1189fee60bfa0e7075ffac4de2e/docs/research/feed-retrieval-slice2a-plan-2026-07-11.html
- Campaign branch: `feat/feed-retrieval-slice2a`

## What to build

Weighted ranking behind a checked-in config, dormant by default. The formula is multiplicative because FTS5 BM25 scores have no absolute scale across queries, so only scale-free multipliers preserve meaning:

```
score = bm25 x tier_mult x aggregator_mult x quality_mult x recency_mult
recency_mult = max(floor, 0.5 ^ (age_days / half_life_days))
```

A new config `feed/config/retrieval-ranking.json` carries `config_ver`, `mode` (`bm25` | `weighted`), tier multipliers, aggregator multiplier, quality multipliers (`ok` / `truncated` / `unknown`; paywall and empty articles are never chunked), and recency half-life plus floor. Provider tier and the aggregator flag come from `feed/config/provider-tiers.json`; quality from the article's stored verdict; age from the chunk's own `published_at`.

Shipping default is `mode: "bm25"` (all multipliers inert) until the benchmark decision (#227) flips it. Every hit's feature log carries every ingredient so the ranking can be multiplied out by hand; the response echoes `mode` and `config_ver` so every run is attributable to a weight set. Doctor validates the config: known keys, multipliers in (0,1], half_life positive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests pin the plan's worked example numerically: bm25 8.0 / tier 1 / 40 days old loses to bm25 9.0 / tier 3 aggregator / 3 days old at half-life 30d, and the ordering flips at half-life 60d
- [ ]
